title: Disney will train Adobe models on its own characters. The tools are for its teams.
friendlyTitle: Disney will use private Adobe models trained on its own characters
summary: Adobe and Disney announced a multi-year alliance on 9 November at Adobe MAX. Disney gets early access to Firefly, Premiere, and Photoshop, and will work with Adobe on models trained on Disney characters, places, and visual styles. Imagineering is already using a sketch-to-image model in its park pipeline. StudioLAB and ESPN are part of the same deal.
friendlySummary: Adobe and Disney announced a multi-year deal on 9 November. Disney's teams get early access to Adobe's creative tools, including models trained on Disney characters, places, and styles. Park designers are already turning sketches into concept art with one of those models.
whyItMatters: This is not a public Disney image generator. It is an internal production tool. Adobe says the outputs are commercially safer because the models are customized on material Disney owns. For anyone else, the useful pattern is a studio training a private model on work it already has, then keeping the result inside its own pipeline.
friendlyWhyItMatters: You cannot use this as a public Disney image tool. It is for Disney's own teams. The useful lesson is narrower: a company can train a private model on work it already owns, and keep the results inside its own process.
